title: Advanced Sequences
source: MindSpark Grade 8 Aptitude & Reasoning | Chapter 1: Advanced Sequences
subtopics: n² + n and n² − n series
Series where differences form a GP
learningGoals: Identify the underlying formula or rule in complex number sequences
Detect and separate two interleaved series from a single sequence
Recognize alternating operations and predict the next term
Verify when successive differences themselves form a geometric progression
Solve IMO/Olympiad-style sequence questions under timed conditions
coreIdeas: Position-based formulas: term T(n) = n² + n gives 2, 6, 12, 20, 30…
Interleaved series: odd positions follow one rule, even positions another — split and treat independently
Alternating ops: +2, ×3, +2, ×3 — apply operations cyclically, track which step you are on
Difference GP: if differences are 2, 4, 8, 16… (ratio 2), you can calculate any term directly
Fibonacci extension: F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2); variants include F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2) + F(n-3)

workedExamples.solution: Odd positions: 3, 9, 15, 21 (+6 each). Even positions: 5, 11, 17, 23 (+6 each). Missing term (7th, odd position) = 15 + 6 = 21. Answer: 21.

beats.teacherLine: Look at this: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30. What do you notice? The gaps are 4, 6, 8, 10 — they increase by 2 each time. That means the differences form an AP. The formula hiding here is T(n) = n² + n. Recognising the difference pattern is the master key to any advanced sequence.
beats.boardAction: Write the sequence 2, 6, 12, 20, 30 across the top. Below, draw arcs showing differences 4, 6, 8, 10. Then write T(n) = n² + n and verify T(1)=2, T(2)=6 in a small table.
beats.checkpointPrompt: Using T(n) = n² + n, what is the 7th term?

beats.teacherLine: Now watch me tackle an interleaved series: 3, 5, 9, 11, 15, 17, ?, 23. First I separate odd positions — 3, 9, 15 — they go +6 each time, so the missing 7th term is 21. Even positions — 5, 11, 17, 23 — also +6. Two independent ladders hidden in one sequence. That's the trap!
beats.boardAction: Write full sequence. Circle odd-position terms in blue: 3, 9, 15, ?. Circle even-position terms in orange: 5, 11, 17, 23. Draw separate ladders for each group. Fill in the blank: 21.
beats.checkpointPrompt: In the series 2, 7, 4, 14, 6, 21, 8, ?, what is the missing term?
beats.fallbackHint: Even positions: 7, 14, 21, ? — they multiply by 7 each term step. Actually each even term = 7 × (position index): 7×1=7, 7×2=14, 7×3=21, 7×4=28.

beats.teacherLine: Your turn. Series: 4, 6, 18, 20, 60, 62, ?. Spot the operation pattern before you guess. Count the steps, label each gap as + or ×, and the rule will jump out at you.
beats.boardAction: Write the sequence. Leave a blank arrow space between each term for the student to label. Show +2 and ×3 labels appearing step-by-step after the student responds.
beats.checkpointPrompt: What is the next term after 62 in the series 4, 6, 18, 20, 60, 62, ?
beats.fallbackHint: Pattern is +2, ×3, +2, ×3 ... . After 62, the next operation is ×3. So 62 × 3 = 186.

sessionFlow.subtopic: n² + n and n² − n series
sessionFlow.coachHook: Can you spot the formula? These aren't random numbers — there's a perfect algebraic rule beneath them.

boardDemo.title: Recognising n² ± n series
steps: Calculate differences: 2, 4, 6, 8 — an AP with common difference 2
Guess formula: T(n) = n² − n. Verify: T(1)=0, T(2)=2, T(3)=6 ✓
boardDemo.teacherLine: When differences form an AP themselves, look for an n² formula. Add or subtract n depending on the starting value.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Say aloud: 'First find the differences, then find the difference of differences.'
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: What is the 8th term of the series 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, 42, ...?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Spot on! T(8) = 64 + 8 = 72. You're reading formulas like a pro!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: T(n) = n² + n. For n=8: 8×8=64, 64+8=72.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Which formula fits the series 0, 2, 6, 12, 20? Write T(n) = ?

sessionFlow.coachHook: The Fibonacci sequence is famous, but Olympiads love its twisted cousins. Let's meet them.

boardDemo.title: Fibonacci variants
steps: Classic Fibonacci: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13 — each term = sum of previous two
Tribonacci: 1, 1, 2, 4, 7, 13 — each term = sum of previous THREE
boardDemo.teacherLine: Always check: is the term the sum of the last 2 or last 3? That one question separates Fibonacci from Tribonacci.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Read this: 'In a Fibonacci variant, identify how many previous terms are summed.'
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: In the series 1, 1, 2, 4, 7, 13, 24, what is the next term?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: each term = sum of previous 3. So 7 + 13 + 24 = 44.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: What distinguishes a Tribonacci series from a Fibonacci series?

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise C: The Hidden Two-Series Trap
sessionFlow.coachHook: This is the #1 Olympiad trap — two sequences disguised as one. Split and conquer!

boardDemo.title: Detecting interleaved series
boardDemo.teacherLine: Whenever a sequence looks irregular, immediately try separating odd and even positions.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Say: 'Odd terms have one rule. Even terms have another rule.'
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: Split — odd positions: 2, 6, 18, ? (each ×3). So ? = 18×3 = 54.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: How many terms does each sub-sequence have when you split an 8-term interleaved series?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Operations can alternate like a pendulum — +k then ×k then +k again. Track the rhythm!

boardDemo.title: Alternating +/× series
boardDemo.teacherLine: Label each gap as + or × before doing any arithmetic. The operation label always comes before the calculation.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Label each operation aloud as you move through the series.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Series: 7, 9, 18, 20, 40, 42, ?. What is the next term?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: The pattern is +2, ×2 alternating. After +2 we get 42, so next is ×2: 42×2=84.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: In an alternating-op series, how do you determine which operation applies to a given position?

sessionFlow.coachHook: When differences multiply instead of adding, the next term explodes. Buckle up!

boardDemo.title: Series with differences in GP
boardDemo.teacherLine: If the differences multiply by a constant each time, you have a geometric difference series. Find the common ratio of differences, extend, and add.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Verify: 2×2=4, 4×2=8, 8×2=16. The differences double every step.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: Find differences — 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 (doubling GP). Add 32 to 33.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: What is the common ratio of the difference series in 1, 2, 5, 14, 41?

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise F: Identify the Rule First
sessionFlow.coachHook: No label given. Classify the series type, then find the missing term. The toughest Olympiad format.

boardDemo.title: Classification before calculation
steps: Step 2: Check if differences are constant (AP), in GP, or alternating
Step 4: Double-check with the known terms
boardDemo.teacherLine: Never rush to guess the rule. Compute differences first, classify second, calculate third.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Read: 'Differences reveal the rule. Always compute them first.'
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Classify and find the next term: 1, 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Spot on! Differences: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 — an AP (d=2). Next diff=11, so 26+11=37.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: differences are 1,3,5,7,9 — odd numbers (AP). Next odd number is 11. Add to 26.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: In the series 1, 2, 5, 10, 17, 26 — what is the type of the difference series?

sessionFlow.coachHook: 20 seconds per question. Olympiad clock is ticking. Go!

boardDemo.title: Speed strategy
steps: Glance at first 3 terms — guess the type
boardDemo.teacherLine: In timed exams, your first instinct after seeing 3 terms should already suggest the rule. Practice builds that reflex.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Challenge: solve each in under 20 seconds.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Boss question — two parts: (a) Find next term in 5, 11, 23, 47, 95, ? (b) Find missing: 4, 7, 13, _, 31, 43
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Outstanding! (a) Rule: ×2+1 → 95×2+1=191. (b) Differences 3,6,_,12 are AP? No — 3,6,8 breaks it. Check: +3,+6,+8,+12 — actually +3,+6,+8 is off. Correct differences: 3,6,9,12,... so missing = 13+8=21.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: For (a) each term = previous×2+1. For (b) differences are 3,6,?→try AP d=3 → next diff=9 → 13+8=21.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: What single test distinguishes a ×2+1 series from a pure ×2 series?

sessionFlow.coachHook: This is Olympiad difficulty. Two concepts in one question. Stay calm, split the problem.

boardDemo.title: Composite sequence challenge
steps: Read the full sequence before computing anything
Check for interleaving first (most common trap)
Combine rule if necessary (e.g., differences of differences form GP)
boardDemo.teacherLine: Elite Olympiad questions layer two patterns. Your job: peel them one at a time.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Breathe and read: identify the pattern type before touching a number.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Masterful! Odd positions: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, ? → ×2 → 32. Even positions: 1, 3, 9, 27, 81 → ×3. Next odd-position term = 32.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: Split into odd and even positions. Odd: powers of 2. Even: powers of 3. 11th term is odd-position = 2^5 = 32.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: In the series 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 9, 8, 27, 16, 81 — what are the two geometric ratios?
